summary: Three pieces of work: two enrichment pipelines repaired (venue geocoding, sports game resolution) and the Supabase migration history rebaselined. All three were failing for the same underlying reason — a dirty or diverged key that made retrying useless.

workstreams.title: Venue geocoding
workstreams.detail: 28 tickets (not 20 as first reported) were dead-lettered with 'no related result'. The provider was never at fault: Nominatim has no API key and returned HTTP 200 every time. It returns an empty result when a venue NAME is mashed with a STREET ADDRESS in one query, and the fallback ladder only ran when the address sat on its own newline — so 26 of 28 venues issued a single unanswerable query.
workstreams.outcome: 19 resolved, 3 correctly classified not-geocodable (a URL, a bare country, a private residence), 7 honest misses. No wrong pins.

workstreams.title: Sports game resolution

metric.label: sports tickets with a resolved game

workstreams.detail: Tickets naming one team never resolved an opponent: parseSingleTeam never returns null, so noisy titles went to the API verbatim and matched nothing. Cleaning the key exposed a worse failure — ambiguous nicknames resolved to the wrong team entirely (Mets -> Puerto Rico, Giants -> Australia).
workstreams.outcome: Venue disambiguates the team, a geography guard rejects impossible matches, and a venue->home-team index learned from resolved tickets handles titles naming no usable team. 11 wrong rows found and removed.

workstreams.title: Supabase migration history

metric.label: matching versions between repo and prod ledger

workstreams.detail: The repo and prod's applied ledger had diverged to 125 files vs 218 rows, with only 28 versions in common. `supabase db push` was unusable, so every migration went in by a route that stamps its own version — widening the gap daily. Verified before acting: replaying the old repo produced 60 tables against prod's 68, so it was a strict subset missing eight admin/ops tables. Repairing the ledger to match it would have made every future branch silently miss them.
workstreams.outcome: Baseline dumped FROM prod (68 tables), 192 files archived, ledger repaired to a single row. `db push` reports 'Remote database is up to date' again. Prod schema untouched; previous ledger backed up.

shipped: Query ladder segments on commas and dashes, not just newlines
Locality is never dropped from a query when the venue supplies one
Typo-tolerant fallback for misspelled venues (Wriggly Field -> Wrigley Field)
URLs, bare countries and private residences no longer enter the geocode queue
Team abbreviations expanded (NYR, D-backs) for both search and verification
Year-less dates placed by weekday inference (Sun, Jul 26 -> 2015-07-26)
Geography guard: a result must be plausible for the ticket's coordinates
Venue -> home team index learned from already-resolved tickets
Migration baseline rebuilt from prod; db push restored

pending.note: Notion Task Queue and raw meeting transcripts were not reachable; the Notion connector is unauthorized. Transcript-derived items do reach Linear via task_extractor, so they are likely represented, but completeness is unconfirmed.

knownGaps: Preview branches replay zero migrations — the project has no GitHub integration connected (SAL2-458)
Branch status reports MIGRATIONS_PASSED over an empty database; assert on table count, never status
eventsday.php returns no venue field, so the venue-anchored sports path resolves through home team only
A right-country but wrong-venue game can still slip through on the team-anchored path
23 of 93 sports tickets remain unresolved, mostly non-team events or titles naming no resolvable team
Eight admin/ops tables reach prod from outside this repo, so schema arrives from more than one source
